provenance.orgName: Battle, Sussex, Benedictine abbey of St Martin
provenance.p: This attribution was rejected in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), which did not change in the Supplement (1987). The corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card, which was originally compiled by Richard Hunt, recorded the following evidence: M G [red] Priscianus Cesariensis in maiori (on vellum strip on front cover, s. xv). The implicit rationale here is that the labelling might point to Battle Abbey -- though Hunt clearly had his doubts, as indicated by his question mark at the top right hand of the card. Ker later rejected the attribution outright, adding the following note to the card: Reject. Continental binding and title. Clasps fasten from second cover to first.
Compare, more recently, the discussion of MS Ff.3.35 in Paul Binski and Patrick Zutshi, Western Illuminated Manuscripts (Cambridge, 2011), p. 384:

The red capitals MG (s. xiii) on the label resemble marks found on the first page of manuscripts from the Benedictine Abbey of St Martin, Battle, Sussex (cf. Kk.6.15), but the attribution has been rejected (MLGB, p. 8; Connolly, p. 121). Similar systems have been recorded in other medieval libraries, for instance at Windsor, and Priscian's Grammar is not among the Battle Abbey books listed by the Oxford Franciscans and John Leland (R. H. and M. A. Rouse, eds. Registrum Anglie, pp. 251-2; R. Sharpe and others, eds. English Benedictine Libraries, pp. 18-22). [For the Connolly citation, see record sources below].
